assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the retailer's tester SHADE CARD press PDF (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered downstream into a live data-merge template).

Document: single card, 55 x 85 mm PORTRAIT, WITH a 3 mm bleed box present on all four edges (media box = trim + 3 mm), fonts embedded. This is the card the retailer's card printer already runs, one per shade tester.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (reads as tidy separate fields):
- Top third: a BOTTLE PICTURE, sitting flush to the top and side trim so it reads full-bleed.
- Beside the name: a round COLOUR SWATCH DOT, filled in the shade's colour, that reads like a little colour-chip well.
- The SHADE NAME, large, in the display face.
- Under it a FINISH line in the text sans (e.g. 'warm honey-amber, sheer').
- A PRICE, '$24'.
- Bottom strip: the INGREDIENT line and the tagline 'Shade first, honestly.', small.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The SHADE NAME, the FINISH line and the PRICE are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame flowing top to bottom, not three addressable frames, and because the sample was built for the one physical shade that story LEADS with the baked word 'Amber Hour', so every field offset has to be reconstructed from the story text past that lead rather than read off the mapping.
- The round COLOUR SWATCH DOT is a DECORATIVE spot-colour vector group (a grouped path), NOT a picture/graphic frame; there is no colour-chip image well anywhere on the card even though it reads like one.
- The only real GRAPHIC FRAME on the card is the BOTTLE WELL at the top.
- The ingredient line and tagline are their own short static story (uniform across all shades, correctly static).

BLEED REALITY: the bottle well is positioned flush to the trim on the top and both sides expecting a FULL-BLEED image, but the cut bottle pictures the imaging surface produces are transparent PNGs centred with margin, so binding a transparent cut leaves a gap in the bleed. A press-ready-with-bleed card can only be honoured by first placing each shade's bottle on the Soft Cream card ground so the image reaches the bleed; a transparent cut bound as-is cannot, and the shortfall must be reported.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): SHADE_NAME | FINISH | PRICE | BOTTLE_PICTURE. (There is NO swatch-picture field: the dot is decorative.)

Colours: Soft Cream #F7F0E6 ground, Warm Ink #3A2A22 name and finish, Brushed Gold #C6A268 rule and price, per-shade colour swatch dot.

assets.defect_engineered: 7 shade rows for the card run, and the traps are: the rows are NOT in the shade-list order so row-1 is not Amber Hour and position names nothing; 'Mulberry Dusk' is drifted to 'Mulberry' so a card named/bound off the raw cell disagrees with the range; prices are formatted inconsistently ($24, 24.00, 24) though all are 24; Clear Dawn (near-clear) has a BLANK Picture cell no header reveals; and Coral Flash's Picture cell is mis-pointed by copy-paste at Peach Noon's cut (shadecard_peach_noon.png), so a naive bind prints Peach Noon's bottle on the Coral Flash card. Picture cells reference the per-shade card pictures cut from the graded masters downstream.
